doc.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Records and big-band trombonists he admired
summary: Influenced by Tommy Dorsey, Goodman, Basie, Ellington and Trummy Young's solo on Margie.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well, we’ve got some specific questions to ask about some of the big groups later on that you played with. Were you influenced by recordings?

Oh, yes. Like during the big band era I guess, the late ‘30’s and early ‘40’s and we always heard the big bands, you know, Tommy Dorsey was a good example of how the trombone ought to sound I guess. He was very popular. And along with oh, Benny Goodman and Count Basie, Duke Ellington. Trummy Young was, I remember that was one of the solos I used to practice on his solo in “Margie” when I was still in high school, with the Jimmy Lunceford band. He sang a chorus and then played a chorus. I think I never heard anybody hit a high F sharp before that.
